transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling today? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for reaching out! I'm feeling okay, but I do have a few questions about my recovery. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing some light gardening, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling, after 1 week of surgery. Just remember to avoid strenuous, heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's great to know, thank you! My next question is: when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should start using preservative-free eye drops four times daily to help with dryness. It's a good idea to get some from the pharmacist and start using them as soon as you can.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, I'll make sure to pick some up. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Yes, it's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, if it's severe or if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. Otherwise, you can try wearing sunglasses when you're outside to help with the sensitivity.
transcript.delivered: Yes, it's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, if it's severe or if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery. But this should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information, Dora. I have no more questions now. I really appreciate your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to assist you. If you think of anything else or have any concerns, don't hesitate to reach out to your care team. Otherwise, I'm glad I could help. .
